summary: Patch special-cases IndexVariables in Dataset.copy to skip the copy that casts '<U*' to object, but it only touches dataset.py while the issue also reports DataArray.copy (ds.z.copy) casting unicode indices — that path lives in dataarray.py and copies coords via v.copy(deep=deep) directly, so it remains broken. Sharing the original IndexVariable object also skips genuine copying (attrs/encoding aliasing) rather than fixing the root cause in IndexVariable.copy.

issues.description: Issue explicitly covers DataArray.copy(deep=True/False) (In[6]/In[7]), but DataArray.copy has its own path copying self._coords with v.copy(deep=deep) and does not route through Dataset.copy. This one-line edit in dataset.py leaves the DataArray case unfixed — incomplete resolution.

Root cause is IndexVariable.copy(deep=True) casting '<U*' to object; correct fix belongs there so all callers benefit. Bypassing the copy entirely returns the SAME IndexVariable object into the copied Dataset, so mutable attrs/encoding become aliased between original and 'deep' copy — a subtle regression versus true copy semantics.
Special-casing at the call site rather than fixing IndexVariable.copy reads as narrowly patched to the failing Dataset path instead of a general fix.
